title: Analytic topology and finite smooth algebraic stratifications of complex varieties
statement:
Let $X$ be a classical algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of [[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]: a separated quasi-compact locally ringed space over $\mathbb C$ with a finite cover by affine models $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the morphisms being the regular maps, i.e. the morphisms of locally ringed spaces over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-morphism-locally-ringed-spaces]]).

(a) **Analytic topology.** An affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ carries the subspace topology of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb C^n$ ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). If $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$ are affine models and $\varphi:Z_1\to Z_2$ is the structure-sheaf isomorphism, then on $Z_1\cap Z_2$ the maps $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$ are given locally by polynomial quotient functions and are therefore continuous for the Euclidean topologies. Hence the topologies transported from the two affine models agree on the overlap, so the affine-model topologies glue to a unique topology on the underlying set of $X$ ([[def-topological-space]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]): the **analytic topology** of $X$. Every regular map of complex classical varieties is continuous for the analytic topologies, and the analytic topology refines the Zariski topology because polynomial zero sets are Euclidean closed. Whenever a complex algebraic variety is used as a topological space below it carries the analytic topology, and each subvariety carries the subspace topology.

(b) **Smooth points.** Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and $x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if its algebraic local ring $\mathcal O_{S,x}$ is a regular local ring: a nonzero Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ satisfies $\dim_{\mathbb C}(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2)=\dim\mathcal O_{S,x}$ ([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]). The residue field at a classical complex point is $\mathbb C$. The variety $S$ is **smooth** if every point is smooth. This intrinsic algebraic condition does not require a Zariski neighbourhood to be algebraically isomorphic to an open subset of affine space.

(c) **Finite smooth algebraic stratifications.** A **finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition** of $X$ is a finite decomposition $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ into pairwise disjoint nonempty connected locally closed subsets $S_\alpha\subseteq X$ - the **strata** - such that each $S_\alpha$, with its reduced induced algebraic structure (locally the polynomial-quotient function sheaf on the locally closed algebraic set), is a smooth algebraic subvariety of $X$, and such that for every $\alpha$ the closure $\overline{S_\alpha}$ of $S_\alpha$ in $X$ is a union of strata. The latter is the **frontier condition**: the frontier $\overline{S_\alpha}\setminus S_\alpha$ of every stratum is a union of strata. An open subset of an affine model is a union of principal open subsets, and each principal open subset is again an affine model, so every locally closed subvariety of $X$ is a classical variety for the induced structure sheaf.
strategy: Every clause is a definition together with its well-definedness check; no existence theorem for stratifications is asserted. (i) Analytic topology: on the intersection of two affine models the transition isomorphism and its inverse are regular, so locally they are polynomial quotient functions, which are Euclidean-continuous; a topology transported along such a homeomorphism is equal to the restriction of the transported topology on the overlap, and the glued topology on $X$ is therefore forced and unique. Continuity of regular maps and the comparison with the Zariski topology (whose open sets are complements of Euclidean-closed polynomial zero sets) are checked in the same local coordinates. (ii) Smoothness is the intrinsic regular-local-ring condition of [[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]] on the algebraic stalk. An isomorphism of classical varieties induces an isomorphism of its local ring, maximal ideal and cotangent space, so the condition is chart-independent. This definition asserts no existence of smooth strata and no analytic-chart comparison theorem. (iii) A locally closed subvariety has its own reduced polynomial-quotient function sheaf; the inverse-image of the ambient structure sheaf is not substituted for that quotient structure. (iii) Strata: a locally closed $S\subseteq X$ is open in its closure, so intersecting the finite affine cover of $X$ with $S$ and using that principal open subsets $D(h)$ of an affine model are affine models exhibits $S$ as a classical variety with the induced structure sheaf. (iv) The frontier condition is a condition on the given finite partition only. No choice principle is used: nothing is selected, and all cited suppliers are choice-free.
axiom_use: None: the definition is choice-free and makes no selection; the cited published suppliers are stated without choice.

title: Analytic field sheaves have injective derived models
statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space $(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$ ([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific injective resolution ([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below injective complexes model the bounded derived category: $K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded derived category are computed by these replacements ([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let $\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition of $X$ ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let $D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then $D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.
strategy: (1) The ringed-space identification makes the published enough-injectives lemma applicable to $(X,k_X)$; its proof supplies local smallness, the Grothendieck axioms and a functorial embedding of every $k$-sheaf into an injective one, and iterating the embedding on the canonical cokernel produces one specific injective resolution with no further selection. (2) These resolutions are bounded-below injective replacements in the sense of the published model theorem, and AC supplies the dependent choice that theorem requires ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]); the equivalence identifies Hom groups in $D^b$ with homotopy classes of maps into the injective models. (3) Closure. Shifts preserve bounded cohomological constructibility. For a mapping cone of $f:A\to B$ constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$, restriction to a stratum $S$ is exact and commutes with finite direct sums and shifts, so $C(f)|_S$ is the mapping cone of $f|_S$. Locally trivializing the finite-rank local systems $H^j(A)|_S$ and $H^j(B)|_S$, the differentials become matrices of locally constant functions; on a small connected neighbourhood such a matrix is constant, so kernels, images and cokernels of the maps induced by $f$ are finite free constant sheaves ([[def-kernel-cokernel-image-sheaves]]). The long exact cohomology sequence of the cone then exhibits each $H^j(C(f))|_S$ as an extension of such local systems. Such an extension is locally split: around a fixed point trivialize the quotient and kernel, lift the finitely many quotient basis germs along the stalkwise epimorphism, represent those lifts by sections on a common neighbourhood, and shrink until their images equal the constant quotient basis sections. Those lifts define a sheaf section of the epimorphism and hence a direct-sum trivialization of the extension. Thus it is locally constant of finite rank; the cone is cohomologically bounded as well. Since the ambient cone triangles make $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ triangulated ([[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]) and a full subcategory closed under shifts and cones is triangulated ([[def-triangulated-subcategory]]), this proves that $D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory; the last sentence repeats the same argument when the two complexes are given with a common stratification. Only steps (1)-(2) use AC, exactly as stated.
axiom_use: AC is used exactly through the functorial injective-embedding theorem for the Grothendieck category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ (which produces the functorial injective resolutions) and through AC $\Rightarrow$ DC for the bounded-below injective model equivalence. The constructibility closure argument is choice-free. No other choice principle is used.

title: Point operations and the open closed constructible line
statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a field. (1) The constructible category of a point is the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, $D_c^b(\operatorname{pt};k)\simeq D^b(k\text{-}\mathbf{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}})$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). For the identity map of the point, all four pullback/pushforward operations $f^*,f_*,f_!,f^!$ are the identity functors of that category, the tensor product and internal Hom are the usual finite cochain constructions, and the dualizing object is $k$ concentrated in degree $0$ ([[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]], [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]]). (2) On the complex line with the open inclusion $j:\mathbb C^*\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$ and the closed inclusion $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, there is a $k$-linear short exact sequence of sheaves
$$0\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to0,$$
and its associated exact triangle is the ordinary localization triangle of the constructible derived category.
strategy: (1) A sheaf on the point is its vector space of sections, so a bounded complex of $k$-sheaves on the point is a bounded complex of $k$-vector spaces, and the single-stratum stratification of the point makes constructibility exactly the condition of finite-dimensional cohomology; a bounded complex with finite-dimensional cohomology is isomorphic in the derived category to a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces (truncate outside the cohomological support and split the resulting finite complex), so $D_c^b(\operatorname{pt};k)\simeq D^b(k\text{-}\mathbf{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}})$ via the injective derived model of [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. The identity map is proper with exact inverse and direct images, so $f^*=f_*=\operatorname{id}$ and $f_!=f_*=\operatorname{id}$ on these categories, and dually $f^!$, being right adjoint to $f_!$, is also the identity; tensor and internal Hom are the signed total tensor and Hom complex of finite-dimensional complexes, and the dualizing object of the $0$-dimensional smooth point is $k$ in degree $0$ ([[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]], [[def-derived-operations-on-analytic-sheaves-over-locally-compact-spaces]]; these two interfaces are declared forward references, closed later in this run). (2) Specialize the published open/closed sequence to the constant sheaf $\mathcal F=k_{\mathbb C}$ ([[lem-extension-by-zero-short-exact-sequence]]): it reads $0\to j_!(k_{\mathbb C^*})\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*(k)\to0$, with $j_!$ the extension by zero of [[thm-extension-by-zero-adjunction-exactness]] and with the sheaf supported at $0$ identified as a pushforward by [[lem-sheaf-supported-on-a-closed-subset-is-a-pushforward]]; exactness is the published stalk computation. The mapping cone of $k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k$ is quasi-isomorphic to $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$ ([[def-mapping-cone-of-a-chain-map]]), so rotating the cone triangle gives $j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}[1]$, the localization triangle of the derived category ([[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]]).
axiom_use: None beyond the assumptions of the cited suppliers: the point and line computations are finite or explicit.
